cards.text: Jeremiah the prophet gets a word from the LORD about the Philistines, Goliath's people (1 Samuel 17:4). Yes, THOSE Philistines. This word comes before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, struck down the Philistine city of Gaza.
The LORD opens with a picture: waters rising from the north, turning into an overflowing torrent. I once overflowed one batch in my oven and thought THAT was a disaster. Friend, I had no idea.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, the torrent from the north overflows only the empty land and leaves the cities alone.
When the torrent overflows the land, what do the people living there do?

cards.text: Everyone in the land is wailing, and it's not water they're hearing. This flood is an invasion on the move, and it's coming FAST.

cards.question: What sound has the people of the land wailing?
With the chariots rumbling in, the Philistine fathers turn back for their sons.

cards.text: The fathers won't turn back, and their hands hang limp. I think that's fear so heavy you can't even lift a finger.

cards.question: The LORD says the day has come to destroy all the Philistines. Who is about to do the destroying?

cards.text: Tyre and Sidon, two cities up the coast, get cut off from every ally they had left, like a whole group chat leaving at once. And the LORD calls the Philistines the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor.

cards.question: Over in Gaza, the people will shave their heads in ___.
In the LORD's word, Ashkelon, another Philistine city, will be silenced.

cards.text: Ashkelon goes quiet, friend. Then the LORD speaks to the few left in their valley, the ones cutting themselves: "O remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourself?"
Then a cry goes up: "Alas, O sword of the LORD, how long until you rest?"

cards.question: What does the cry beg the sword of the LORD to do?

answers.text: Go back in its sheath and be still
Strike once more and finish fast

cards.question: The sword of the LORD can't rest, because the LORD has ___ it.

cards.text: The LORD has appointed that sword against Ashkelon and the shore of its coastland. That's His word on the Philistines, friend, and it's a heavy one.

findings.problem: The story card before card 6 says "it's not water they're hearing." That rules out the wrong answer "Thunder and crashing waves" before the baker picks. "This flood is an invasion on the move" also points straight at the horses and chariots, so the card all but gives away card 6's answer.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The comparison "like a whole group chat leaving at once" doesn't share the core action. In the text, the allies of Tyre and Sidon are cut off as part of the LORD destroying the Philistines. People leaving a group chat choose to walk away, so the image doesn't line up with being destroyed. It also makes a light joke out of a people being wiped out.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The text is a prophecy in the future tense: "will overflow," "will wail," "will not turn back," "will be silenced." Several cards retell it in the present tense as if it is happening now. Card 7 says "the Philistine fathers turn back," card 10 says Tyre and Sidon "get cut off," and card 13 says "Ashkelon goes quiet." Card 12, in contrast, keeps "will be silenced." Storyteller present tense may blur what was foretold with what took place.
findings.question: In prophetic passages, may Papa Dorin retell the foretold events in storyteller present tense, or must cards keep the prophecy's future tense ("will") so they don't present a prediction as an event already happening?
